All that you need to know about Debug & Deploy - techFEST'26

For Non-SLIET Participants Only,

techFEST'26 is North India's premier technical festival, organised by Sant Longowal Institute of Engineering and Technology (SLIET), Longowal, Punjab. This is a paid opportunity with the early-bird packages mentioned below:

Non-SLIET participants must register through the official techFEST’26 website to avail accommodation and other event perks.

Register Now: https://www.techfest26.com

 

DEBUG & DEPLOY

We cordially invite you to Debug & Deploy, an exciting technical competition organised as part of techFEST’26, the Annual Technical Festival of Sant Longowal Institute of Engineering & Technology (SLIET).

This event is designed for participants who enjoy technology, logical thinking, problem-solving, and programming. It provides an opportunity to compete with talented minds, test your technical abilities, and experience challenges inspired by real-world software development.

About the Event

Debug & Deploy is a three-round technical competition that takes participants from fundamental technical knowledge to practical programming and debugging.

Each round is designed to test a different skill set. Participants will begin by demonstrating their understanding of computer science concepts, move on to a technical word puzzle that challenges their observation and reasoning abilities, and finally enter the Debugger's Arena, where they will identify and fix errors in buggy code.

The competition is not just about knowing how to code; it is about understanding problems, thinking logically, identifying errors, and finding effective solutions.

Number of Rounds: 3

 

Round 1 – Tech Quiz

The competition begins with Tech Quiz, a round focused on testing participants' fundamental technical knowledge.

Participants will answer multiple-choice questions based on basic computer science and technology concepts. The questions are designed to evaluate conceptual clarity, technical awareness, logical thinking, and understanding of fundamental computing topics.

  • 25 Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs)
  • Duration: 30 minutes
  • Coverage: Basic Computer Science and Technology
  • Questions will test conceptual understanding and technical awareness.
  • Participants will be ranked based on their performance.
  • Top scorers will qualify for Round 2.

This round provides the foundation for the competition and tests how well participants understand the concepts behind the technology they work with.

Round 2 – Word Puzzle

The second round, Word Puzzle, challenges participants to combine their technical knowledge with observation, vocabulary, logical thinking, and problem-solving skills.

Participants will be presented with a grid containing hidden technical words and terms. The objective is to carefully analyse the grid, identify the relevant technical terms, and find them accurately.

  • Challenge: Find technical words hidden within the given grid.
  • Duration: 30 minutes
  • Scoring: Based on both accuracy and speed.
  • Participants must carefully observe the grid and identify the maximum number of relevant terms.
  • Top performers will qualify for the final round.

This round tests not only technical familiarity but also attention to detail and the ability to recognise patterns quickly.

Round 3 – The Debugger's Arena

The final round is The Debugger's Arena, where participants put their practical programming and debugging skills to the test.

Participants will encounter a collection of beginner-level buggy code snippets containing common programming mistakes. These may include syntax errors, logical errors, incorrect conditions, or other issues that prevent the program from producing the expected output.

The objective is to carefully analyse each program, identify the source of the error, make the necessary corrections, and ensure that the code produces the correct output.

  • 15–20 beginner-level buggy code snippets
  • Duration: 1.5 hours
  • Task: Identify and fix errors in the given programs.
  • The corrected programs must produce the required output.
  • The round focuses on debugging ability, logical reasoning, programming fundamentals, and accuracy.
  • Final Ranking: The overall final ranking will be based solely on performance in Round 3.

This round simulates real-world programming scenarios where developers are often required to analyse existing code, identify problems, and implement precise fixes.

Final Challenge

The first two rounds will serve as qualification rounds, testing participants' technical knowledge, observation, and problem-solving abilities.

The participants who qualify will enter The Debugger's Arena, the decisive final round. Although performance in the first two rounds determines who reaches the finale, the final positions and winners will be decided exclusively by performance in Round 3.

Participants will need to demonstrate not only their ability to understand code but also their ability to think critically, locate errors, implement solutions, and deliver correct results.

Think. Debug. Deploy.

Are you ready to find the error, fix the code, and prove your technical skills?

Tests passed (40%), time taken (30%), quality of fixes (20%), successful deployment (10%).

Website: www.techfest26.com | Email: techfest@sliet.ac.in

Rules and Regulations - General Rules:

  • All participants must carry a valid college ID card and their techFEST'26 registration receipt.
  • Reporting time will be communicated to registered teams; late reporting may lead to walkover.
  • The decision of the judges and organisers will be final and binding in all matters.
  • Any form of misconduct, plagiarism or use of unfair means leads to immediate disqualification.
  • Participants are responsible for their own equipment and personal belongings.
  • Organisers reserve the right to modify any rule at any time; updates are announced at the venue
  • Individual event; systems with required tooling are provided.
  • Stack Overflow is off, official docs are on.
  • Rewriting the entire project instead of debugging leads to penalty

Eligibility:

  • Open to students of all institutes and all degree programmes (unless specified otherwise in the event rules above).
  • Participants must be registered for techFEST'26 through the official portal.
  • Cross-college teams are welcome.

 

Prizes:

1st place: Winner trophy/certificate and cash prize

2nd place: Runner-up certificate and cash prize

3rd place: Certificate and cash prize

Certificates of participation for all registered participants.

 

Why You Should Participate:

Debug & Deploy is more than a competition - it is a platform to test your skills against the brightest minds from institutes across the region, learn from judges and mentors, and build memories that last far beyond the festival. Winners take home cash prizes, trophies and certificates that strengthen their resumes, while every participant leaves with experience, exposure and connections. Whether you are a seasoned competitor or a first-timer, the arena at techFEST'26 welcomes you.

 

About the Festival - techFEST'26 at SLIET:

techFEST'26 is the annual technical festival of Sant Longowal Institute of Engineering and Technology (SLIET), Longowal, Punjab - a deemed-to-be university under the Ministry of Education, Government of India. Established in 1989, accredited with Grade A by NAAC, SLIET spreads across a lush 451-acre campus with 11 departments and more than 5,000 students. With a legacy of over 28 years, techFEST'26 - themed 'Technology and Sciences for Sustainable Earth' - features 50+ events across 11 clubs and a total prize pool of Rs 5,00,000+, along with workshops, exhibitions, guest lectures and a grand cultural evening.

 

Festival Highlights at techFEST'26:

  • 50+ technical, non-technical and cultural events across 11 clubs
  • Total prize pool worth Rs 5,00,000+
  • Grand cultural evening and pro-shows
  • Hands-on workshops, exhibitions and expert guest lectures
  • Early-bird registration packages for participants from all institutes.

Accommodation and Meals:

Registration for the techFEST’26 package is compulsory for accommodation and other perks, while participation in individual events is free*.

 

Code of Conduct:

  • Maintain discipline and decorum across the campus and all event venues.
  • Indiscipline or misbehaviour with volunteers, organisers or fellow participants leads to disqualification.
  • Consumption of alcohol, tobacco or any intoxicants is strictly prohibited on campus.
  • Participants must not damage institute property; recovery costs may be charged.
  • Organisers reserve the right to remove any participant violating the code of conduct.

Refund and Cancellation Policy:

The registration fee, once paid, is non-refundable under any circumstances. In case an event is cancelled by the organisers, registered participants will be accommodated in an alternative event where feasible.

How to Prepare:

Read the event rules above carefully and prepare accordingly. Carry your own stationery, chargers and any personal equipment mentioned in the rules. Reach the venue at least 30 minutes before your reporting time, and follow the official techFEST'26 social media handles for last-minute updates and announcements.

How to Reach SLIET:

Sant Longowal Institute of Engineering and Technology is located at Longowal, District Sangrur, Punjab - well connected by road and rail. The nearest railway stations are Dhuri and Sangrur; the institute is a short taxi/bus ride from either. Ample parking and signboards guide visitors to the festival venues inside the campus.

 

Frequently Asked Questions:

  1. Who can participate in techFEST'26 events?
  2. Students of any institute and any degree programme can participate, provided they register through the official portal.

 

  1. Is accommodation available for outstation participants?
  2. Yes - choose the Rs 499 package for on-campus hostel accommodation during the festival.

 

  1. Can students from different colleges form one team?
  2. No, single participation only not a team event.

 

  1. Will participation certificates be provided?
  2. Yes, every registered participant receives a participation certificate; winners receive trophies, cash prizes and certificates of merit.

 

  1. What if an event's timing clashes with another event I registered for?
  2. Inform the event organisers at the help desk; schedules are adjusted wherever possible.

 

  1. Whom should I contact for queries?
  2. Reach out to the overall coordinators listed below or write to techfest@sliet.ac.in.

 

  1. Do I need to bring my own equipment?
  2. Only where the event rules above specify; everything else is provided by the organisers.

 

  1. Can I participate in multiple events during the festival?
  2. Yes - your single techFEST'26 registration covers participation across all events, subject to event schedules.

 

 

Indicative Event Day Schedule:

  • Reporting and verification: 30-45 minutes before the scheduled start
  • Participants' briefing and rules walkthrough by the event head
  • Competition rounds as described above, with short breaks between rounds
  • Results announcement and prize distribution at the venue, shortly after judging

Exact timings for each event are shared with registered participants over email/SMS and at the help desk. Keep an eye on the official social media handles for the final schedule.

Awards and Recognition:

Winners and runners-up receive trophies and cash prizes as per the prize details above, along with certificates of merit. All participants receive e-certificates of participation. Outstanding performers may also get the opportunity to be featured on the official techFEST'26 social media handles and be considered for future flagship events at SLIET.

 

Safety and Fair Play Policy:

 

techFEST'26 is committed to a safe, inclusive and fair competition environment. Every event is supervised by faculty coordinators and trained student volunteers. First-aid support is available on campus throughout the festival. Any participant found violating safety instructions, tampering with equipment, or engaging in unfair practices will be disqualified and escorted out of the venue. Report any concern to the event head or the help desk immediately - your safety comes first.

 

Terms and Conditions:

  1. Participation in techFEST'26 events implies acceptance of all the rules mentioned above.
  2. The organisers hold the right to use photographs and videos of the event for promotional purposes.
  3. Prize money is distributed after the completion of the festival, post verification of winners.
  4. In case of any dispute, the decision of the festival convenor shall be final and binding.
  5. All disputes are subject to the jurisdiction of courts at Sangrur, Punjab.

 

For Queries and Updates:

Naman Kumar Sinha (Overall Coordinator): +91 78568 93952

Shubham Kumar Singh (Overall Coordinator): +91 97711 74465

Email: techfest@sliet.ac.in | Website: www.techfest26.com

Follow us on Instagram and other social media platforms for updates.

 

Prepare yourself for a journey of technology, creativity and celebration.

 

Mark your calendars and be part of the magic of techFEST'26 at SLIET!
